page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.r5 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.r5.xlarge operates in the lower tiers for compute and memory throughput. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1105.68 and a multi-core score of 2937.38, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block cached speed of 164.23 GB/sec, but uncached large block read-only bandwidth drops to 20.9 GB/sec, which is categorized in the bottom 10%. Similarly, Redis SET operations perform at 2.85 million operations per second, and single-threaded gzip compression registers at 19.17 GB/sec, reflecting poor relative performance.

Given its high memory allocation relative to compute power, the ecs.r5.xlarge is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance CPU execution. The instance is suitable for caching layers, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring a larger memory footprint. However, the weak CPU and memory bandwidth benchmark results represent a significant tradeoff, suggesting that computationally intensive tasks, high-throughput web serving, or large-scale data processing may experience bottlenecks on this hardware configuration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with a KVM hypervisor, this instance offers a dedicated CPU allocation with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates weak to poor performance across CPU and memory bandwidth tests, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 2937.38 and uncached large block memory read bandwidth at 20.9 GB/sec. Consequently, the ecs.r5.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive but computationally light workloads, such as caching systems, small database instances, or basic enterprise applications requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without demanding high processing throughput.
